answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x and explicitly confined to the primary region, which matches the March regional-degradation pattern more closely than a fleet-wide release or a pure capacity miss. memory_b2 reports failover restored latency in minutes with a clean traffic shift, which serves the objective of sustained availability without dropping customer writes. A release did ship ~30 minutes before the climb, so rollback (memory_b1) remains a live alternative and should be verified before a hard commit; I am not treating the release as proven causal. Circuit breaking is rejected because failing writes at settlement peak would lose customer writes. Read-replica routing and extra capacity are weaker fits for a region-scoped write-path failure and can wait. Peak settlement means failover still carries downstream consistency/settlement risk, so keep this a standard guarded shift rather than an unguarded broad cutover until the two archives confirm the playbooks.
